newsitem.title: UK: DMG recommends Russia's Tatneft over Chernogorneft. [CORRECTED 11:03 GMT]
newsitem.headline: DMG recommends Russia's Tatneft over Chernogorneft. [CORRECTED 11:03 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects headline to read that DMG recommends Tatneft over Chernogorneft, rather than Chernogorneft over Tatneft)
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell is recommending investors shift from Russian oil company Chernogorneft to Tatneft ahead of an issue of American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) by the latter.

"This may seem a strange moment to be recommending Tatneft barely a month after it was targetted by the Russian bankruptcy commission for non-payment of tax," Deutsche said in its daily Russian report.

It says that the case against Tatneft occured due to an oversight at the Ministry of Finance and as it has western accounts and a western audit of reserves yet trades at half the value of Chernogorneft, valuations are compelling.

With a market capitalisation of $663 million, Tatneft is valued at 10.8 cents per barrel of reserves and $3.61 per barrel of 1996 output, compared with 24.1 cents and $6.90 respectively for Chernogorneft.
Deutsche notes that investors have been blissfully unaware of the Tatneft ADR and the Tatarstan government releases 10 percent of equity in December this creates a buying opportunity.

"We think it makes good sense to take profits as the Chernogorneft ADR picks up on the good political news (Yeltsin's heart operation) - and to put the money in to buying Tatneft underlying," DMG said.
